turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. You're thirty weeks, ja. What's the problem today.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, thirty weeks. Um, it's my legs at night. They creep, and then I can't sleep.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Both legs?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, both. When I lie down. I don't know, doctor, it's weird.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Since when.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Err...
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Days or weeks.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know. Maybe three weeks, could be more. I really don't know, doctor.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Painful?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Not pain exactly. Like crawling, and I have to kick them. Uh.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Swollen?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit, evenings. By morning it's...
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Chest pain or short of breath.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain. Not short of breath.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Calves red or hot.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No they're not.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hours of sleep.
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Maybe four. I walk the passage. My husband gets...
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Daytime.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja I'm wrecked. I nod off. I do admin at the municipality, shame.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): And the parking there is a mess this week, but ja.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Folic acid and iron. Yes or no.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): The yellow folic ones, five milligrams, every morning. Ja.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Iron.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): The red iron tablets. I don't know the proper name, doctor, bottle's at home. I think two hundred milligrams?
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): How often.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Once a day, after supper. If they make me queasy I skip. Not every night, hey.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Other medicines.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Umm, midwife is Tuesday morning at the clinic. That's booked.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Keep Tuesday. Sister's card, pressure one oh nine over seventy-seven, pulse ninety-two.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): They said it was higher before, I think. I don't know.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Last pressure was one-forty over eighty-eight. Today's is one oh nine over seventy-seven. That one counts.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Chart temp thirty-seven point two. No. Corrected, thirty-six point eight. Weight seventy-one point four kilos.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that weight ok? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fine. Ferritin in August was eleven. Low. Likely why the legs creep.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): So the tablets aren't even working?
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Not proven. Thursday morning the sister takes bloods, fasting, full blood count and ferritin. Hold the red tablet till after. Yellow folic you take with water.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): And if it comes back sort of middle-ish...
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): If those are borderline we do the third test, transferrin saturation. Not otherwise.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): If the creeping doesn't go, though. I don't know.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): If it does not settle, a leg scan. Not booked now.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll see you in two weeks with the results. Passage walk is fine. No extra tablets from the chemist.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. Two weeks then. Hope I sleep.

spec.situation: Pregnant woman at 30 weeks with creeping legs at night and poor sleep; ferritin discussed; takes folic acid and iron; midwife check booked.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: interruptions_trailing_off: people interrupt each other, trail off, or the answer comes two turns after the question.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
